learningObjectives: Explain the importance and benefits of mobile test automation.
Install and configure Tosca Mobile and TMA for testing readiness.
Explore local and cloud-based connection options in Tosca Mobile.
Capture and interact with mobile app elements using scanning options.
Execute reliable and scalable mobile tests using Tosca Mobile.

elements.term: Original course and local study track
elements.description: The Academy introduction is a 45-minute course developed with Tosca 2024.2. Its five topics cover getting started, installing Tosca Mobile and TMA, connection options, scanning options and execution options. This local track expands that outline with platform preparation and troubleshooting; the additional lessons are independent study material, not the Academy syllabus.

Mobile automation covers native apps, mobile websites and hybrid apps with embedded web content. A framework name alone does not determine whether an app is hybrid: React Native can produce native controls. The current guide distinguishes Mobile Engine 3.0 and Mobile Web Engine 3.0 scanning/steering paths.

elements.text: The Academy lists software-testing and mobile-automation knowledge, AS1 training, access to Tosca with a valid Tosca Mobile license, access to TMA, and Android Studio setup as prerequisites. Check compatibility and entitlement for your installed versions.

bulletPoints: The Academy introduction has five topics; the local track adds deeper platform and troubleshooting material.
Native/hybrid/web apps differ in preparation, controls and opening/steering paths.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What you will be able to do

elements.title: Academy outline and independent extensions
items: Academy Topic 1 — Getting Started with Tosca Mobile automation.
Academy Topic 2 — Installing Tosca Mobile and Tricentis Mobile Agent.
Academy Topic 3 — Overview of connection options.
Academy Topic 4 — Overview of scanning options.
Academy Topic 5 — Overview of execution options.

Independent extensions in this local track — Android/iOS preparation, detailed connection and TestCase authoring guidance, advanced Modules and troubleshooting. These are not additional topics in the introductory Academy course.

bulletPoints: The Academy course has five topics. Its summary covers mobile benefits, setup, local/cloud connections, scanning and execution.

elements.text: The Academy knowledge, training and technical prerequisites are listed below. Additional target-preparation guidance comes from the versioned public manuals; it extends the introductory course.

elements.title: Academy training prerequisite
items: Tricentis Tosca Fundamentals — Automating web application testing (AS1).

elements.title: Technical prerequisites
items: Academy prerequisite: access to Tricentis Tosca, including a valid license for Tosca Mobile. Confirm current entitlement and training-license availability with the official provider.
Academy prerequisite: access to the Tricentis Mobile Agent.
Academy prerequisite: download and set up Android Studio.
Additional local readiness guidance: at least one supported Android target, prepared according to the installed Agent version’s requirements.
For the TMA 2025.4 support matrix, iOS targets require a macOS Agent host and compatible Xcode. Check the installed Agent version’s requirements.

elements.text: TMA 2025.4 lists iOS hosting as macOS only. A Windows Tosca workstation can connect remotely to the supported Mac Agent. Older guides describe different host support; do not turn one version’s requirement into a timeless claim or assume Tosca Commander runs natively on macOS.

bulletPoints: Verified Academy prerequisites: testing/mobile knowledge, AS1 training, licensed Tosca Mobile access, TMA access and Android Studio setup.
Android targets may use a supported Windows Agent host.
For TMA 2025.4 iOS, use a supported macOS Agent host reached remotely from the Tosca workstation.

elements.description: Prepare components, devices and connections before scanning and executing. This follows the documented workflow; it is not evidence that a particular percentage of lessons or most real-world failures concern setup.

elements.text: Validate each layer with its logs and configuration. A scan success or device listing does not prove every execution prerequisite is satisfied.

bulletPoints: Avoid diagnosing a failure from one symptom alone.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing this course with AE1's Mobile Engine lesson
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming everything already covered by AE1's single mobile lesson is all there is to know.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Academy introduction has five topics covering getting started, installation, connection, scanning and execution. This local track adds platform-specific preparation and advanced operations; do not mistake those extensions for the original introductory syllabus.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to automate iOS from a Windows-only setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing TMA on Windows and expecting to scan an iOS app or simulator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TMA 2025.4 requires a macOS host for supported iOS operation. Connect the Windows Tosca workstation remotely to that Agent; check installed-version requirements rather than assuming universal support.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does this local mobile track expand the AE1 mobile introduction?

options.text: It uses a different automation engine entirely.
It adds detailed platform preparation and advanced Module/troubleshooting guidance to the introductory mobile workflow.
It only covers mobile web testing, not native apps.
It replaces the need for a Tosca licence.

practiceQuiz.hint: A broader local outline, with the applicable Mobile and Mobile Web engine paths.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The local track develops setup, platform preparation, connections and the wider mobile workflow. It does not introduce an unrelated engine or replace licensing.

optionExplanations.A: The local track develops the same mobile automation concepts rather than inventing an unrelated engine.
optionExplanations.B: This describes the local extension. The verified Academy introduction itself has five topics from getting started through execution options.
optionExplanations.C: Native and hybrid apps are included alongside mobile websites.
optionExplanations.D: A study track does not remove product licensing or access requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Windows Tosca workstation uses the TMA 2025.4 support matrix, with no Mac host available. Which listed target can it automate if other prerequisites are satisfied?

options.text: Neither Android nor iOS — a Mac is required for all mobile automation.
Android automation, using a physical device or an Android Studio emulator.
iOS automation only, via the iOS Simulator on Windows.
Both platforms equally, since TMA abstracts away the OS difference.

practiceQuiz.hint: Xcode — and therefore the iOS Simulator and iOS device automation — only runs on macOS.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA 2025.4 supports Android hosting on Windows and lists iOS hosting as macOS only. This is version-scoped support, not proof that every historical or future Agent has the same restrictions.

optionExplanations.A: The TMA 2025.4 matrix permits Android hosting on Windows.
optionExplanations.B: Android devices/emulators are supported on an appropriate Windows host when preparation and compatibility requirements are met.
optionExplanations.C: An iOS simulator requires the supported macOS/Xcode environment in this matrix.
optionExplanations.D: Bundled setup does not override the Agent host/platform support matrix.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why does the documented mobile workflow prepare components, devices and connections before scanning and executing tests?

options.text: Because Mobile Engine 3.0 requires more TestSteps than other engines.
Because scanning and execution depend on a prepared, supported environment and connection.
Because setup lessons count double toward the Final Exam.
Setup is optional and can be skipped by experienced learners.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about where confusing failures actually originate in mobile testing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Preparation establishes prerequisites needed for scanning and execution. The manuals do not quantify the fraction of course lessons or real-world failures caused by setup.

optionExplanations.A: Preparation is about prerequisites, not a fixed higher TestStep count.
optionExplanations.B: A supported prepared target and configured connection are prerequisites for the later workflow.
optionExplanations.C: No verified exam-weighting rule is established here.
optionExplanations.D: Experience does not remove necessary device and connection prerequisites.

quickRecap.value: Independent local outline covering Mobile Engine 3.0, Mobile Web Engine 3.0 and TMA: setup, platforms, connection, scanning and authoring.
The local track extends introductory mobile material. Academy course 1311 has five topics; the additional local lessons are independent extensions.
Native, hybrid and mobile web apps require their applicable scanning/steering path; the framework name alone does not determine app type.
Academy prerequisites: software-testing/mobile-automation knowledge, AS1 training, licensed Tosca Mobile access, TMA access and Android Studio setup. Check installed-version compatibility separately.
TMA 2025.4 iOS support uses a macOS Agent host; a Windows Tosca workstation connects remotely.
Preparation → connection/scanning → configuration/authoring/execution. No asserted percentage of lessons or failure causes.
Academy course 1311 was developed with Tosca 2024.2; local technical supplements use Tosca 2026.1 and TMA 2025.4. Do not merge these version requirements.
